the appearance of light nuclei substantially lowers the critical density of the liquid-gas phase transition in supernova matter.

the appearance of light nuclei in the supernova envelope substantially changes the properties of the equation of state and that the appearance of the light nuclei substantially lowers the critical deuterium condensation temperature.

the composition of supernova matter in the density range {rho} {approx} 10{sup -4}-10{sup -3} g/cm{sup 3} is substantially affected by the presence of light clusters and that the appearance of these clusters lowers the critical temperature of the deuterium condensation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the composition and thermodynamic properties of low-density supernovae matter, which may be important for the dynamics of the supernova explosion.
the composition of supernova matter and the equation of state of supernova envelopes.
the properties of light nuclei in supernova matter and the role they may play in the evolution of supernovae and proto-neutron stars.

the quasipartcle-gas model with the Skyrme functional provides a reasonable description of light nuclei in low-density supernova envelopes.
light clusters in supernova matter are important and should be taken into account.
the presence of clusters in the supernova envelope has a substantial impact on the equation of state and on the composition of matter.

the presence of light nuclei substantially modifies the properties of low-density supernovae matter.
